question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass safely; on one-way streets, drive to the nearest road edge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, you should begin the turn from:
options: a:Make the turn from any lane, providing you signal well in advance.,b:Make the turn from the rightmost lane.,c:Make the turn from the leftmost lane.
note: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you intend to go (leftmost lane) and enter the nearest appropriate lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most often:
options: a:Increases your ability to react to a hazard.,b:Does not increase the chance of a crash.,c:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.
note: Speeding is a leading factor in crashes and typically leads to riskier decisions that increase crash severity.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
note: Lower your headlights to low beams when following closely to avoid blinding the driver ahead and to reduce glare.

question: What is the nighttime driving curfew for 16- and 17-year-olds (effective Aug 1, 2008)?
options: a:10 p.m. to 6 a.m.,b:11 p.m. to 5 a.m.,c:12 a.m. to 5 a.m.
note: 16- and 17-year-old drivers are generally prohibited from driving between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. unless exceptions apply for work, school, religious activities, or medical necessity.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Wait until the truck or bus turns before you turn.,c:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.
note: Do not try to cut between a large vehicle and the curb while it is turning; wait until it completes its turn.

question: What does safe interstate driving require of motorists?
options: a:Have the ability to safely drive at increased speeds.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Both of the above.
note: Interstate driving requires drivers to handle higher speeds safely and stay constantly alert for traffic and roadway hazards.

question: What important action should you take before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Check traffic in all directions.,c:Always move to the left lane.
note: Before turning, check traffic to the front, rear, and both sides to ensure the maneuver can be made safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red arrow pointing to the right on a traffic signal means you may:
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means no turning in the arrow direction until a green signal or arrow permits the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection controlled by a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light functions like a stop sign: stop, yield to others, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper method to make a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and move into the lane nearest the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and move toward the centerline before turning.,c:Approach in the left lane and swing wide.,d:Signal only if other traffic is present.
note: Signal, slow, and approach the turn from the lane nearest the right curb or edge, staying close to the curb.

question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Slow down or change lanes to create a gap.,c:Honk to alert them to merge.,d:Speed up to pass them quickly.
note: When safe, merge into another lane or slow to create a gap so entering vehicles can merge smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
note: Passing on the shoulder is unsafe and illegal; only pass where the roadway permits and it is safe to do so.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Signal when pulling next to a curb and when pulling away so other drivers understand your intentions.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.,b:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,c:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.
note: If stopping on the shoulder, turn on emergency flashers and remain in the vehicle if it is safe to do so; walking along an interstate is hazardous.

question: When following a motorcycle, allow extra space in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:Passenger vehicle.,b:Station wagon.,c:Motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see, so give them additional space to respond safely.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:All of the above.,c:Alertness and concentration.
note: Alcohol and many drugs reduce alertness and concentration, slow reaction times, and impair coordination.

question: What is the effect of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Excessive speed greatly increases the chance of severe crashes and is a leading contributing factor in fatal collisions.

question: With oncoming traffic to your left and parked cars to your right, steer:
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,c:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
note: Maintain a middle course between oncoming traffic and parked cars to maximize clearance on both sides.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how fast should you be traveling?
options: a:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.,c:At the legal speed limit.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of the existing traffic so you can merge smoothly, unless that speed exceeds the legal limit.

question: What defensive action should you take when driving at night?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase following distance when visibility is reduced at night and use headlights correctly to improve safety.

question: When traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.,b:Make room for the merging traffic if possible.,c:Always maintain your exact position.,d:Move onto the shoulder to let them in.
note: When safe, make room to let merging vehicles enter the lane smoothly rather than asserting right-of-way aggressively.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow arrow warns that the protected left-turn phase is ending and drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: If you start to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Open a window.,b:Drink something with caffeine.,c:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
note: To avoid fatigue-related crashes, stop and rest or switch drivers; short fixes like caffeine or an open window aren't reliable.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintaining a steady speed.
note: Maintain a steady speed and signal well in advance to help the driver behind keep a safe following distance.

question: Stopping distances and crash severity:
options: a:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,b:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the likelihood of more severe crashes; adjust speed to conditions.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid left, what steering action should you take?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left (into the skid).,b:Turn the steering wheel to the right (away from the skid).,c:Keep the steering wheel straight and not turn.,d:Brake hard immediately.
note: If the rear skids left, steer left (into the skid) while easing off the accelerator; with ABS, brake firmly while steering.

question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, a motorist should:
options: a:Continue ahead. The motorist has the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians within crosswalks and wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.,d:You are always safe to drive if the label does not warn against driving.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can impair driving ability; it is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug that affects your driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you come to an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down, be alert, and proceed through the intersection with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic before merging?
options: a:Using your rearview and side mirrors only.,b:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your rearview mirror only.,d:Using the horn to alert others.
note: Use side mirrors and a shoulder check to view blind spots and ensure it's safe to merge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never take when changing lanes?
options: a:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Do not change lanes or attempt to pass by crossing the centerline within an intersection; wait until clear and legal to do so.

question: In a vehicle equipped with airbags, the safest place for children 12 and under is:
options: a:The front seat.,b:The back seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under should ride in the back seat because airbags can be dangerous for smaller passengers.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what is the safest choice before driving?
options: a:Loudly play the radio while driving so you won’t think about your argument.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Emotions affect driving ability; calm down before driving so you can focus on the road and make safe decisions.

question: In bad weather, what is the correct steering and braking approach?
options: a:Steer off the road immediately.,b:Steer and brake smoothly.,c:Brake sharply and steer quickly.,d:Use hard steering corrections to avoid hazards.
note: In inclement weather, make gradual steering and braking inputs to maintain control.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent is associated with what change in crash risk?
options: a:Won't put other drivers at risk.,b:Won't have any effect on your driving.,c:Will double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even small increases in BAC significantly raise crash risk; a BAC of 0.02 can substantially increase the likelihood of a collision.

question: At dawn or dusk and during rain or snow, a good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:
options: a:Up the instrument panel lights.,b:On your parking lights.,c:On your headlights.
note: Use your headlights when conditions make it hard to see or be seen; use low beams when wipers are required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the first available lane on the one-way street.,b:Turn into any lane.,c:Turn into the far right lane.,d:Turn into the second lane from the curb.
note: When turning onto a one-way street, enter the lane nearest to you that is lawful and available (the first lane).

question: What defines a crosswalk?
options: a:Another name for a four-way intersection.,b:An area designated for road construction workers.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the designated area — marked or unmarked — where pedestrians may legally cross the street.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.,c:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
note: Give motorcycles a full lane; never share the same lane or crowd a motorcycle when passing.

question: When driving in fog, which of these is the correct practice?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights; high beams will reflect and reduce your forward visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making a left turn must yield to which traffic?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Passing cars.,c:No one in particular.
note: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic, including bicycles and motorcycles, that are close enough to be a hazard.

question: Which action commonly blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Rubbernecking at crashes or unusual events slows traffic and contributes to congestion and secondary crashes.

question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection.,b:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,c:Drive to the left and stop.,d:Remain stopped until the vehicle passes.
note: If in an intersection, clear it and then pull to the right and stop to yield to the emergency vehicle.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on city streets?
options: a:To see potential hazards early.,b:Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop at any speed.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.,d:Because lane markings are harder to see.
note: On freeways you should scan farther ahead to detect hazards sooner and have more time to react to changing traffic conditions.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:A good idea if the weather is bad.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can create hazards as other drivers may attempt unsafe passing maneuvers.

question: Why should you never use high beams when driving in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: High beams reflect off fog, snow, or rain and worsen visibility; use low beams and fog lights where equipped.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:Only if a crossing guard is present.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians using white canes or guide dogs must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: To be able to turn quickly, your hands should be positioned:
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel (e.g., roughly 9 and 3 o'clock) to maintain control during turns.

question: How must you treat a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane must always be given the right-of-way.

question: A driver should keep watch over which areas around the vehicle?
options: a:Only directly in front.,b:Beside, ahead, and to the rear of the vehicle.,c:Only the rearview mirror.,d:Only in the direction of travel.
note: Safe driving requires scanning ahead, to the sides, and behind to be aware of all hazards.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction on water (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.,c:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.
note: If you start to hydroplane, ease off the accelerator, slow down gradually, and do not apply the brakes suddenly.

question: When parking on any hill, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your front wheels parallel to the road regardless.,b:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park.,c:Leave the vehicle in neutral to relieve brake pressure.,d:Always point the wheels toward the center of the road.
note: Always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park; turn wheels toward/away from the curb depending on uphill/downhill parking.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle in the roadway, what is the safest action?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,c:Shift into neutral while driving through it.,d:Speed up to create a wake and drive through.
note: Avoid deep puddles to reduce the risk of skidding and loss of control; dry, solid pavement is the safest driving surface.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to scare them away.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Slow down and proceed carefully as animals may bolt into the road unexpectedly; avoid swerving suddenly.

question: Which action can reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Always signal when changing lanes.,c:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,d:Tailgate slower drivers to encourage them.
note: Signaling your intentions when changing lanes helps prevent misunderstandings and reduces road rage occurrences.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Drive carefully through without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.,d:Treat it as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,b:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,c:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
note: If possible, get your vehicle completely off the road, put on emergency flashers, and make it visible to other drivers.

question: If bad weather reduces your visibility, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Increase your following distance during poor visibility to allow more time to react to hazards.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and is blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look ahead toward the left edge of your lane.,b:Look ahead toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look straight ahead in your lane.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights; look toward the right edge of your lane and use peripheral vision to track the vehicle.

question: Regulatory road signs are commonly what color background?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:White.,d:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs notify drivers of laws and are typically white rectangles with black, red, or green letters/symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when should you reduce your speed?
options: a:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,b:As you approach the deceleration lane.,c:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
note: Keep your highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the advisory speed for the exit.

question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you scan?
options: a:Left, your right, then your left again.,b:Left.,c:Right.
note: Look left and right for approaching vehicles and pedestrians, then left again because left-approaching vehicles are closer.

question: No passing zone signs and markings indicate:
options: a:There are oncoming cars passing in your direction.,b:Passing is only permitted during daylight hours.,c:You cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.
note: A no passing zone means your sight distance is limited or conditions make passing unsafe; do not pass there.

question: For persons age 21 or older, what BAC level is illegal for driving?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: It is illegal for drivers 21+ to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,c:Brake hard and steer sharply to the right.,d:Immediately turn off the engine and coast.
note: On a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator to slow, and steer to a safe place out of traffic before braking heavily.

question: What should you do to reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed on wet roads to reduce the chance of hydroplaning or losing traction; avoid sudden steering or braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light requires you to slow down and proceed carefully; you do not need to stop unless necessary for safety.

question: How should you proceed when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,d:Maintain your current speed.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are continually being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane highways, keep right unless passing or preparing for a left turn; move right if you are impeding traffic.

question: When you are following a motorcycle, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Allow a larger following distance.,c:Be ready to use your horn.,d:Maintain your usual close following distance.
note: Allow at least a three- to four-second following distance behind motorcycles because they can stop quickly and are more likely to fall on slippery surfaces.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, how should you proceed?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.,d:Ignore them unless they step into the road.
note: Slow and proceed cautiously when pedestrians are near the road, being prepared to stop if needed.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and remove alcohol's effects from your body?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Time.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to metabolize alcohol and eliminate its impairing effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, whom must you yield to?
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic.,d:Only yield to vehicles, not pedestrians.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Neither lane may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing or crossing from either direction.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive slowly enough to stop within the illuminated area of your headlights.,b:Turn on high beams to better see ahead.,c:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be seen.,d:Drive at the posted daytime speed limit only.
note: At night drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed in a no passing zone, what should you do to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter the lane safely?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: Slow down slightly to give the passing vehicle room to return to the lane safely; do not speed up or swerve.

question: If you parallel park facing downhill, you should:
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: a:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,b:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: Increase your following distance and do not tailgate in work zones; expect lane shifts and slower traffic.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: Remove your foot from the accelerator to increase the gap without abruptly braking or swerving, reducing crash risk.

question: A broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline means you may cross to pass on the left when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,d:When the passed driver flashes their lights.
note: Return to the right lane when you can see the front (headlights) of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror; always signal first.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When another driver makes a mistake.,b:When it may help prevent a collision.,c:To encourage slow drivers to move faster.,d:To greet friends on the sidewalk.
note: Use the horn only to avoid collisions or warn others of immediate danger, not to express frustration.

question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you avoid using?
options: a:Cruise control.,b:Lower gears downhill.,c:Gradual steering inputs.,d:Increased following distance.
note: Never use cruise control on snow or ice because it can cause loss of vehicle control; make gradual changes and increase following distance.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
note: Large vehicles have big blind spots on both sides; avoid lingering alongside them so the driver can see you.

question: Why should motorists give extra space to children riding bicycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,b:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children on bicycles are often less predictable, have slower reflexes, and are harder to see; give them extra room and caution.

question: Is it legal to drive while using medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:Yes, if it is prescribed by a physician.,b:Only if you do not feel drowsy.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:Only on short trips.
note: Driving under the influence of any substance that impairs ability is illegal; impairment can come from prescriptions, OTC meds, or illegal drugs.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, you should not:
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace against the back of your seat and press your head into the head restraint to reduce whiplash.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change as speed increases?
options: a:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,b:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,c:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the force of impact, raising the risk of serious injury or death.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign indicate to drivers?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To speed up slightly.
note: A No Passing Zone sign indicates that passing is not permitted in the marked area because it is unsafe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you NOT do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and return from there.,b:Back up on the road or shoulder.,c:Find an alternate route beyond the exit.,d:Proceed to the next crossroad to turn around.
note: Never back up on the freeway or shoulder; continue to the next exit and safely return to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing, what should you confirm?
options: a:That the passed vehicle signaled for you to return.,b:That you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:That you are one vehicle length ahead.,d:That the passed vehicle slowed down.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection at the posted speed when the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,b:Speed up to cross the intersection before the light turns red.,c:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow light warns the signal will soon turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs impair coordination, alertness, reaction time, and concentration — all essential for safe driving.

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than during the day?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility and glare from headlights limit how far you can see at night; use headlights and drive cautiously.

question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?
options: a:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,b:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription and over-the-counter drugs — including cold medicines, sedatives, and some cough syrups — can impair driving; know how your medication affects you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: When passing, do so promptly and safely, and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed?
options: a:Driving down long, gradual hills.,b:Driving up long or steep hills.,c:Driving on level roads.,d:While passing smaller vehicles.
note: Large trucks often slow when climbing long or steep hills because they need more power to ascend.

question: Which of the following substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving; always know the effects of medications you take.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning left on red is legal only when:
options: a:You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,b:You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.,c:You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: After a complete stop, you may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless signs forbid it.

question: What behavior describes defensive driving?
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.,c:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving means continuously scanning the road, checking mirrors, and anticipating potential hazards.

question: When stopping on snow or ice while driving a vehicle with ABS, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the system will modulate the brakes automatically to prevent wheel lockup.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action is prohibited?
options: a:Looking over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Checking for drivers entering the same lane.,c:Moving into another lane while inside an intersection.,d:Signaling before changing lanes.
note: Never change lanes while in an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal.

question: How close may you park to a fire hydrant?
options: a:Within 15 feet.,b:Within 10 feet.,c:Within 20 feet.,d:Within 5 feet.
note: Do not park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant at any time to allow access for emergency services.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a left turn when turning from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, start from the lane nearest the left curb and turn into the first legal lane available.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you must:
options: a:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians before completing a left turn; go only when the way is clear and signals allow.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,b:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:Alcohol affects judgement, which is needed to drive safely.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment even at low levels; being below the legal limit does not guarantee unimpaired driving.

question: To be aware of traffic behind you, you should:
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.
note: Regularly scanning your rearview and side mirrors keeps you informed of the speed and position of traffic behind you.

question: What must you do when you approach an eight-sided (octagonal) sign?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Stop completely at the sign.,c:Turn if the way is clear.,d:Yield and proceed without stopping.
note: An octagonal sign is always a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way, then go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a red light is showing but a green arrow is also displayed, when may you proceed in the arrow direction?
options: a:First come to a complete stop.,b:Wait until the light changes.,c:Are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the proper lane and do so safely, yielding to anyone in the intersection.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign indicates:
options: a:Yield.,b:Stop.,c:Warning.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special conditions or hazards ahead; they are usually yellow or orange.

question: You should always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town that has frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.
note: Never stop on the tracks; only cross when you can completely clear the other side. Expect trains on any track at any time.

question: What is a likely effect of tailgating another vehicle?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Reduces collisions by preventing being 'cut off.',c:Cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Following too closely can provoke other drivers, increase risk, and may lead to traffic citations for unsafe driving.

question: From top to bottom, what is the proper order of traffic lights?
options: a:Green, yellow, red.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Red, yellow, green.,d:Yellow, red, green.
note: Traffic lights are ordered red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permitted to pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken (dashed) line beside your lane means passing is permitted when it is safe to do so.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots can be eliminated with one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked using your rearview mirror alone.,d:Mirrors always show everything around your car.
note: Large trucks have significantly larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles; mirrors do not eliminate blind spots entirely.

question: Approaching a steady yellow light at an intersection, what should you do if you have not entered the intersection?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce speed and prepare to stop if safe.,c:Come to a safe stop.,d:Increase your speed and proceed.
note: A steady yellow light warns the signal will soon turn red; if you haven't entered, stop safely before the intersection.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in fog.,b:Constantly staring at the road ahead.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,d:Driving with only parking lights on.
note: Regularly check rearview mirrors to stay aware of traffic; do not use high beams in fog.

question: To check a blind spot before changing lanes, where should you look?
options: a:Only the inside rearview mirror.,b:Over your left or right shoulder to view the blind spot.,c:Only the left outside mirror.,d:Only the left-side window.
note: Look over the appropriate shoulder to check blind spots that mirrors cannot show when changing lanes.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When they are wet after several hours of rain.,c:When they are clean and dry.,d:During freezing temperatures only.
note: Roads tend to be most slippery just after rain begins as oil and debris mix with water to form a slick surface.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow centerlines on roads?
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate lanes moving in the same direction.,d:Mark bicycle lanes.
note: Broken yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is allowed when safe.

question: By how much should you reduce your speed when driving on packed snow?
options: a:One-third.,b:One-quarter.,c:One-half.
note: On packed snow, reduce your normal speed by about half to maintain control and allow for longer stopping distances.

question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams will reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: Combining a prescription drug with alcohol can:
options: a:Make you more alert.,b:There will likely be no effect.,c:Make you unfit to drive.
note: Mixing alcohol with certain medications can intensify impairment, making you unsafe to drive.

question: You should always travel at:
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At the speed limit.
note: Adjust your speed to weather and road conditions while obeying posted speed limits; never exceed the legal limit.

question: Which of the following statements about seat belt use is false?
options: a:They prevent a 'human collision' by holding you in place.,b:They are not necessary if your vehicle has an airbag.,c:They keep you from being thrown from the vehicle in the event of an accident.
note: Seat belts are required even in vehicles with airbags; airbags alone do not provide full protection in many crash scenarios.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following persons' instructions must drivers obey?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Drivers must follow instructions from authorized traffic control personnel such as flaggers to protect workers and other road users.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your visibility, you should drive more slowly and turn on your:
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Turn on headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly so other drivers can also see you.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,b:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.,c:You must stop when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Use caution near tracks.

question: Which is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.,d:Driving below the posted work zone speed.
note: In work zones, do not follow too closely and remain attentive to workers and equipment; both tailgating and inattention are hazardous.

question: What happens as your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More sober.,c:More coordinated.
note: A higher BAC means increased impairment of coordination, judgment, and reaction time, i.e., greater intoxication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit should be driven only under which conditions?
options: a:During the day.,b:During the night.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The maximum posted speed is the fastest safe legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust speed for traffic, weather, and road conditions.

question: If you drive too fast on a wet road, what danger may occur?
options: a:Your tires will start to glide over the water.,b:Your ability to judge speed and control will be impaired.,c:Your own spray will obscure the vision of other drivers.
note: At higher speeds on wet roads, tires can ride on a film of water (hydroplaning), causing loss of control.

question: What should you do when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.,b:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.,c:Visibility is better than on pavement.
note: Loose surfaces offer less traction; you must slow down, allow longer stopping distances, and avoid sudden movements.

question: If you reach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Slow down and drive around the gates.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.,c:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
note: Stop behind the lowered gates and wait until lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: If you are under 21, your license may be suspended after driving with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:0.08 percent or more.,b:Any amount.,c:0.15 percent or more.
note: Connecticut enforces a zero-tolerance policy for drivers under 21; any measurable alcohol can lead to suspension.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:Through vibration and sound, they alert inattentive drivers that their vehicles have left the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips produce noise and vibration to warn inattentive or drowsy drivers that they're drifting off the roadway or approaching a hazard.

question: What is the safest response if you encounter an aggressive driver?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up.
note: Avoid confrontation: yield space and let an aggressive driver pass or move away to reduce the chance of conflict or a crash.

question: Which area is most likely to be icy after snow or rain on cold days?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Shaded portions of the roadway often freeze first and thaw last; be cautious in shaded areas during cold, wet weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You enter a left-turn lane for an upcoming turn and see oncoming traffic. What should you do first?
options: a:Move to the left of the center lane.,b:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,c:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.
note: Signal about 100 feet before turning and keep your wheels straight until you're ready to turn to avoid being pushed into traffic.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do at an intersection?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:Continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go, but you must yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

question: How can sudden highway wind gusts affect vehicles?
options: a:They generally affect only large vehicles.,b:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,c:They only reduce visibility.,d:They have no effect on vehicles.
note: Strong winds can destabilize vehicles of any size and may also reduce visibility by blowing dust or debris.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Traffic next to the broken yellow line may cross to pass when safe; traffic next to the solid line may not pass.

question: How should you approach the right-of-way rules when driving?
options: a:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
note: Never assume you have the right-of-way; be prepared to yield if doing so prevents a collision.

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.,c:Keep your wheels facing straight.
note: When parking uphill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the road's edge so the vehicle will roll off the roadway if it moves.

question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot in the direction you plan to move.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway in bad weather, how should you follow?
options: a:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.,b:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,c:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.
note: Give trucks extra space when following so you can see around them and so the truck driver can see you; tailgating large vehicles is dangerous.

question: Which action helps prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet pavement; reduce speed to maintain tire contact with the road.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Construction and maintenance warning signs.,b:General warning signs.,c:Red.
note: Orange is used for construction and maintenance warning signs and devices; exercise special caution in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: Never pass in intersections or where your view is blocked by a curve or hill. Pass only where signs or pavement markings indicate it is legal and safe.

question: What message appears on a red octagonal sign?
options: a:One-way.,b:Do not enter.,c:Stop.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) red sign always means STOP — come to a complete stop at the sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles to your right and left arrive simultaneously, yield to:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: When multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle when:
options: a:Where there is a red traffic light.,b:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must obey steady or flashing red signals and always follow directions from officers directing traffic.

question: If you must park in an area not normally used for parking, you should:
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: When parking off the normal area, position your vehicle so it is visible to approaching drivers to avoid creating a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and have not entered it, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce you speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon turn red; if you haven't entered the intersection, stop safely.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly to slow down.,c:Pull over immediately onto the roadway without slowing.,d:Speed up to reach the shoulder.
note: Keep control by holding the wheel, easing off the gas, and braking lightly; then pull off the road when safe.

question: From which areas of your vehicle must you remove snow, ice, and frost before driving?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors so you have clear visibility before driving.

question: A steady red arrow on a traffic signal means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits traffic from proceeding in the arrow's direction until a green signal appears.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c:Only when you are slowing down.
note: Frequently glance at your rearview and side mirrors to stay aware of traffic around you rather than staring fixedly ahead.

question: What color are traffic control devices and signs used in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Orange.,c:Red.
note: Orange is used for construction and maintenance warning signs, cones, and barriers; use extra caution in work zones.

question: If your car becomes disabled while on the highway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway, if possible.,c:Stop where you are.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, move it completely off the main-traveled portion of the roadway and turn on emergency flashers.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to judge distance and speed; you can only see as far as your headlights allow.

question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Never. It confuses other drivers.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Often, even at controlled intersections.
note: Yield your right-of-way whenever doing so reduces the chance of a crash; never assume others will yield.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, how should you slow the vehicle?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and immediately.,b:Tap or pump the brakes lightly.,c:Slow down gradually by easing off the accelerator and use brakes lightly.,d:Turn off the ignition to stop quickly.
note: On a blowout, ease off the gas to slow gradually and use the brakes lightly once speed has reduced.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy conditions, you should:
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Slow down in wet conditions; higher speeds increase the chance that tires will ride on top of water and lose traction.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags:
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,c:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.
note: Airbags supplement seat belts; for best protection use lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.

question: If your vehicle's rear starts skidding left, which way should you steer?
options: a:Steer to the left (into the skid).,b:Steer to the right (away from the skid).,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,d:Turn the wheel sharply the opposite direction of the skid.
note: If the rear skids left, steer left into the skid to help realign the vehicle and regain control.

question: In a motor vehicle on a highway, what is the law regarding open containers of alcohol?
options: a:Illegal to either drink from or possess open containers of alcohol.,b:Legal to drink alcohol if you're not driving.,c:Legal to drink alcohol if you're driving but not drunk.
note: It is illegal for occupants to possess or consume open alcohol containers in a motor vehicle on a highway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can create hazards as other drivers may make dangerous passing maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.,c:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.
note: Before changing lanes or merging, check behind and to the sides and then watch the vehicle ahead to enter safely.

question: As you approach the crest of a hill, you should:
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Prepare to stop, if needed.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: Because you cannot see what is on the other side of a hill, reduce speed and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: If you are 16 or 17 and convicted of driving more than 20 mph over the speed limit, your license will be suspended for:
options: a:30 days.,b:45 days.,c:60 days.
note: A first offense for a 16- or 17-year-old driving 20 mph over the limit results in a 60-day license suspension plus fines and restoration fees.

question: If you are in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If it is safe and possible, move vehicles out of traffic to avoid blocking the roadway and reduce the risk of secondary collisions.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road and use lane markings to guide your vehicle until the blinding headlights pass.

question: A double solid yellow centerline means that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow line down the center of the road indicates that passing is prohibited in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your original lane?
options: a:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,b:See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

question: If heavy smoke covers the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on high beams and continue.,b:Reduce speed, move right, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and proceed slowly.,d:Speed up to get past the smoke.
note: If the road ahead is covered by heavy smoke, slow down, move right, and stop off the roadway until it is safe to continue.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn sharply to re-enter the road.,b:Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and gently brake.,c:Speed up and re-enter quickly.,d:Immediately swerve back onto the pavement.
note: If your vehicle leaves the roadway, hold the wheel steady, ease off the gas, gently brake, then check traffic and re-enter when safe.

question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead when you:
options: a:Are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space ahead (don’t brake suddenly) or change lanes to reduce the collision risk.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait near the vehicle for the owner.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,d:Drive away and report it later.
note: If you damage a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, leave a note with your contact information securely attached to the vehicle.

question: A solid yellow line beside a broken yellow line means that:
options: a:Driving in both directions may pass.,b:The lane next to the broken line may pass.,c:The lane next to the solid line may pass.
note: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe; a solid line means passing from that side is prohibited.

question: Which ability is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Balance.,b:Judgement.,c:Vision.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment early, reducing your ability to make safe driving decisions.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and not brake.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow, and brake gently only if needed; pull off when safe.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a stop sign?
options: a:30 feet,b:25 feet,c:15 feet
note: Do not park within 25 feet of a stop sign; parking restrictions help maintain visibility and traffic flow.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue slows reactions, impairs judgment, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel, increasing crash risk.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur when:
options: a:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Driving substantially faster or slower than the flow of traffic increases your risk of collision.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, drivers must:
options: a:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.,b:Stop if you are driving in the same direction.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: You must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children, regardless of which direction you are traveling, unless otherwise directed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn explicitly not allowed?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,d:At a four-way intersection with a traffic signal.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic; visibility is limited and collisions can result.

question: What is the only thing that lowers blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Time
note: The only way to sober up is to allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol; nothing else accelerates this process.

question: What should you do prior to entering a curve?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control; braking while turned can cause skidding.

question: At about what speed can tires begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:As low as 35 mph.,b:Around 45 mph.,c:About 55 mph.,d:Only above 60 mph.
note: Tires may begin to hydroplane at speeds near 35 mph when they cannot channel water away from the tread.

question: Which of the following factors affects how alcohol is absorbed in an individual?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Alcohol absorption is affected by weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and the number of drinks consumed; time is required to eliminate it.

question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you in the city. What should you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.
note: Pull to the right edge of the roadway and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless you are in an intersection, in which case clear it first then stop.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,c:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.
note: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars; pedestrians or drivers can step or pull out without warning.

question: When driving at night, you should:
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance and use low/high beams appropriately to avoid blinding others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle traveling the same direction, it is safe to return to the right lane when:
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Only move back into the lane when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror; also check blind spots.

question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposing traffic; you may pass when the dashed line is next to your lane and it is safe.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.,d:You may pass only on the left.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

question: There is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead. What should you do?
options: a:Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.,b:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, you must yield to pedestrians in your lane and allow them to cross safely.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: If the broken line is on your side, you may pass when safe; if the solid line is on your side, passing is prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:
options: a:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match traffic speed and merge smoothly with freeway traffic rather than stopping.

question: Like alcohol and other drugs, how can drowsiness affect your driving?
options: a:Help you be a better driver.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness reduces reaction time, awareness, and judgment much like drugs or alcohol, making driving unsafe.

question: On the highway, looking far ahead of your vehicle helps you do what?
options: a:Spot upcoming police officers.,b:Reduce need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Keep up with traffic speed.,d:See the license plates of distant cars.
note: Scanning far ahead lets you anticipate hazards and reduce abrupt maneuvers, smoothing your driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but there is no gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and force the other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.
note: If no safe opening exists, slow on the acceleration ramp to find a gap you can merge into safely.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,c:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop more quickly than cars and require extra following distance so you have time to react if they brake suddenly.

question: Construction zone signs are generally what color and shape?
options: a:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
note: Temporary work-zone signs have an orange background with black wording or symbols to warn drivers of construction.

question: Which is true about traffic in work zones?
options: a:Drivers do not need to obey traffic signs.,b:Traffic patterns can change daily.,c:Traffic patterns usually remain the same.,d:Speed limits are always increased.
note: Traffic patterns in work zones can change frequently, including lane shifts and alternating lane closures, so stay alert and follow signs.

question: If a vehicle's suspension is failing, what problem is most likely to occur?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Flat tires.,d:Battery drain.
note: The suspension system helps you control the vehicle and a poor suspension can cause handling and control problems.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror.
note: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check blind spots that mirrors do not show before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving next to a dashed single white line, you may:
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: A broken white line separates lanes going the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes if safe.

question: If no reduced speed signs are posted in a work zone, what speed should you follow?
options: a:You should obey the normal speed limit.,b:You should drive 15 mph slower than the posted speed limit.,c:You should drive 15 mph faster than the posted speed limit.
note: If a work zone does not post a reduced speed, follow the normally posted speed limit for that road.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:That the child will be in total control.,b:The child may make unpredictable movements; expect the unexpected.,c:That the child will obey all traffic laws.,d:That the child will always yield to cars.
note: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable; slow down and be prepared for sudden movements.

question: To avoid conflicts with merging traffic from on-ramps on an interstate, what is the best action?
options: a:Change lanes to the left.,b:Slow down.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: Move to the left lane when safe and traffic permits to allow merging vehicles space to enter from the right.

question: Blue traffic signs typically provide information about:
options: a:Motorist services.,b:Construction and maintenance.,c:Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.
note: Blue road signs are service signs that indicate motorist services like rest areas, food, lodging, and hospitals.

question: At a crosswalk, drivers must:
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to you.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks; where signals are absent, vehicles must stop for pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a Yield sign, you should:
options: a:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,b:Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,c:Should slow down but never stop.
note: Drivers must be prepared to stop at a yield sign and give way to traffic that could conflict with their movement.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take some caffeine pills.,b:Try to fight it.,c:Take a break.
note: If you become drowsy, stop at the first safe opportunity to rest, nap, stretch, or switch drivers — caffeine pills are not a substitute for sleep.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through an intersection despite a red light, you should:
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Go through the intersection without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: Follow the directions of a police officer directing traffic; their instructions override traffic signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a broken yellow centerline between two lanes of traffic mean?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you may cross to pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat an intersection when the traffic signal is not functioning?
options: a:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,b:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: Treat an intersection with no working signals as an all-way stop: stop, then look and yield before proceeding unless directed otherwise by an officer.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Start to prepare to slow down and, if necessary, sound a sharp blast of your horn.,c:Drive faster to pass before they get there.,d:Ignore them unless they step out.
note: If a child is about to enter the street, prepare to slow immediately and sound a sharp horn blast if needed to warn them.

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,b:Inconvenience drivers.,c:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
note: These devices delineate safe paths and keep vehicles away from construction hazards and workers.

question: Having a driver license is considered a:
options: a:Right, not a privilege.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Requirement.
note: A driver's license is a privilege granted by the state, not an inherent right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but a police officer signals you to stop, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,c:Obey the officer.
note: Drivers must follow lawful directions from police officers even if those directions differ from traffic signals or signs.

question: An orange-and-red triangular emblem on the rear of a vehicle indicates what?
