options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:Slow-moving vehicle.,c:The vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: Slow-moving vehicles (e.g., tractors or horse-drawn vehicles) display an orange-and-red triangular reflector to warn other drivers.

question: When must you obey directions from a school crossing guard?
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:Unless you do not see any children present.,c:At all times.
note: Be alert near schools and always follow the instructions of crossing guards to protect pedestrians.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Which of the following best describes the thinking of a defensive driver?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and prepare to respond to avoid collisions.

question: When approaching someone crossing with a white cane or guide dog, how should you respond?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Honka horn as you pass.,c:Stop until the person is well clear of your path.,d:Proceed slowly while they cross.
note: Yield and stop until a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog is safely out of your path.

question: What color and lettering do temporary construction and maintenance signs have?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Orange background with black writing.
note: Temporary work-zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of construction or maintenance ahead.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Use the brakes lightly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and use the brakes lightly if needed while slowing and pulling off the road safely.

question: Which foot should be used for both braking and accelerating in most vehicles?
options: a:Use your left foot for braking.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,c:Alternate feet when braking suddenly.,d:Use left for accelerating and right for braking.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake; apply brakes smoothly with increasing pressure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited from your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start the turn from:
options: a:Any lane (as long as it is safe).,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:The lane in the center of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto a one-way street, begin from the far left lane and turn into the far left lane.

question: To avoid glare from an oncoming vehicle's headlights, you should:
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stay focused on the centerline on the road.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road briefly to avoid direct glare, then resume scanning the road ahead.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its signal arm extended, you should:
options: a:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,b:Proceed at normal speed, but watch for children.,c:Stop.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm until the arm is retracted and the bus moves.

question: What should you do if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Open a window.,c:Stop to rest or change drivers.
note: If you feel tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers; fatigue slows reactions and impairs judgment.

question: If your car starts to skid out of control, what should you do first?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.,d:Turn off the engine immediately.
note: If you skid, avoid braking; steer to regain control until the vehicle is stable again.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a Yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign you must give the right-of-way to crossing or merging traffic close enough to create a conflict; stop if necessary.

question: If the road is slippery, adjust your following distance to be:
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther from the car ahead than normal.,c:Closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: Slippery roads increase stopping distances, so leave extra space between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.,b:Increase the volume of your radio.,c:Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.
note: If you notice signs of fatigue (e.g., drifting lanes, heavy eyelids), stop in a safe place and rest or take a short nap.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds your stopping distance increases; look well ahead to give yourself more time to react.

question: You should allow an extra cushion of space when following which vehicle?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,c:When following a small passenger car.
note: Give larger vehicles or those towing trailers extra space because their drivers may have limited rear visibility and they block your sight of the road ahead.

question: If a green light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear it quickly.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Stop immediately where you are.,d:Back up out of the intersection.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed to clear it safely.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Whenever you need to use them.,b:Before you get into the car.,c:Before you start driving.
note: Adjust your seat and mirrors, fasten your safety belt, and secure items before moving your vehicle — do not adjust mirrors while driving.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway, even if a crosswalk is not marked.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy conditions?
options: a:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.,b:Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.,c:Slow down.
note: Lower your speed in wet conditions to reduce the chance your tires will lose contact with the road and cause hydroplaning.

question: Which behavior may identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:The number of passengers in their car.,b:Their erratic and improper lane changes.,c:Their tendency to drive slowly.,d:Using turn signals consistently.
note: Aggressive drivers often make improper or erratic lane changes; avoid challenging them and get out of their way.

question: What does a red-painted curb generally mean?
options: a:Loading zone.,b:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red curb indicates that stopping, standing, or parking is prohibited.

question: What should you do before switching on your vehicle's ignition?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Make seat belt use part of your routine: buckle up and ensure passengers do the same before starting the vehicle.

question: Which factor commonly contributes to crashes?
options: a:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,b:Scanning the environment regularly.,c:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.,d:Driving at the general flow of traffic.
note: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions is a common crash factor; remain within speed limits and adjust for conditions.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Follow closer than you would a passenger car.,b:Follow farther back than you would a passenger car.,c:Drive on the truck's right side and wait to pass.,d:Pass quickly on the right.
note: Large trucks have larger blind spots and longer stopping distances; maintain extra following distance behind them.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Brake abruptly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake lightly.
note: Do not apply the brakes during a skid; steering into the skid and easing off the gas helps regain control.

question: Which statement about motorcycle, scooter, and moped operators is correct?
options: a:Are easy to see and are predictable.,b:Must share a traffic lane with another vehicle.,c:Have the right to use a complete traffic lane.
note: Motorcyclists and similar riders are entitled to a full lane; do not crowd them and allow full lane width when passing.

question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:At all times.
note: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in crosswalks whenever pedestrians are present regardless of other factors.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, you should:
options: a:Look straight ahead.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.
note: Look toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while still keeping enough view of the road to steer safely.

question: How might a bicyclist behave when making a left turn?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists may occupy the leftmost lane or otherwise position themselves appropriately when preparing to make a left turn; expect them to behave like motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road you should:
options: a:Sound your horn as you pass.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Always judge the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles before passing; wait if you are unsure there is enough time and space.

question: What is true about fines for speeding in work zones?
options: a:They are not enforced.,b:They can be doubled or increased.,c:They can always be argued in court successfully.,d:There are no extra penalties.
note: Fines and penalties in work zones can be greater than normal, and distracted-driving fines may also be increased.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you make a right turn where lane markings or signs do not control turning?
options: a:Turn from any lane.,b:Turn from the right lane.,c:Speed up to provide room for vehicles behind.
note: When no signs or markings control turns, turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to travel and enter the closest legal lane.

question: Drivers aged 16 or 17 are prohibited from using which devices while driving?
options: a:Text messaging device.,b:Both of the above.,c:Cell phone.
note: Drivers 16–17 may not use any cell phone or mobile electronic device while driving; violations can lead to license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,c:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
note: It is illegal to pass in marked no passing zones or over railroad crossings and in other locations where passing is prohibited for safety reasons.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not start to cross an intersection if doing so will block it after the light turns red under which condition?
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely to avoid blocking traffic even if the signal is green when you enter.

question: In traffic traveling 50–55 mph you are least likely to crash if you:
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.,c:Stay within that speed range.
note: Traveling at a speed consistent with the flow of traffic helps prevent collisions, provided speeds remain legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is correct about checking blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.,b:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.,c:You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and glance over the appropriate shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Are traveling in the wrong direction.,b:Must treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,c:May not proceed until it changes to green.
note: A flashing red light should be treated exactly like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever acceptable to drive off the paved road to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: Never leave the main-traveled portion of the roadway to pass another vehicle; doing so is illegal and unsafe.

question: Which statements about driving speed are true?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.,b:As your speed increases, so should your following distance.,c:Both of the above.
note: Higher speeds increase crash severity and stopping distance; increase following distance as speed increases.

question: After several beers, what will reduce the effects of alcohol on your system?
options: a:Taking a cold shower.,b:Waiting several hours.,c:Drinking several cups of coffee.
note: Only time reduces BAC; other measures like coffee or a cold shower do not speed the elimination of alcohol.

question: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles so you can:
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,c:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
note: Large vehicles block forward sight and have larger blind spots; increase distance to see the road ahead and allow reaction time.

question: A driver's license is considered which of the following?
options: a:A right.,b:A privilege.,c:A requirement.,d:A guarantee.
note: Driving is a privilege that can be suspended or revoked for unsafe or unlawful behavior.

question: When poor visibility is caused by rain or fog, which lights should you turn on?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Interior dome light.
note: Use low beam headlights in rainy or foggy weather so others can see you; high beams reduce visibility by reflecting back.

question: Using the steering wheel as a clock face, where should a driver's hands be placed?
options: a:9 and 3 o'clock.,b:11 and 4 o'clock.,c:9 and 12 o'clock.,d:8 and 2 o'clock.
note: Hands are commonly recommended at 9 and 3 o'clock for control; some guidance suggests slightly lower positions for comfort and safety.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: At places where people may cross or where lines of traffic meet, look to the left and right to ensure no one is approaching.

question: When you drive through a construction zone, you should:
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Pass the construction zone carefully and not “rubberneck.”
note: Do not slow down to stare at accidents or work zones; pass carefully, obey the posted signs, and maintain a safe following distance.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross where you are turning right, what should you do?
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,b:Wait until the person has crossed before turning.,c:Turn off your engine until they cross.,d:Proceed slowly and honk to warn them.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes must always be given the right-of-way; wait until they are safely across.

question: Why is extra space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Trucks require longer stopping distances than cars; leaving extra space in front gives the truck room to stop safely.

question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously.
note: Time is the only way to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC); coffee, showers, or exercise do not lower BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you park uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Right, toward the side of the road.,c:Left, toward the center of the road.
note: On hills without a curb, turn the wheels toward the side of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?
options: a:No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.,b:Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.,c:Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.
note: Driving too slowly can obstruct normal traffic flow and may result in a citation; adjust speed appropriately.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the left.,b:Permitted from the right.,c:Not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean no passing from either direction because they separate opposing traffic.

question: An orange-colored road sign indicates:
options: a:There is roadwork ahead.,b:You must change lanes ahead.,c:There is a detour ahead.
note: Orange signs are used to indicate construction or maintenance work zones; proceed with caution.

question: When a large truck makes a right turn on a multi-lane street, what may it do?
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Long vehicles often swing wide during right turns to prevent their rear wheels from clipping the curb or objects; give them extra room.

question: Roads with a double solid yellow centerline indicate that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is prohibited in both directions.

question: When visibility is reduced by rain or fog, which lighting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Fog lights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams can reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Never make abrupt or spontaneous lane changes; always check mirrors and blind spots and signal before moving.

question: When is it inappropriate to use your horn?
options: a:If it may help prevent a collision.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:To warn another driver of imminent danger.
note: Avoid using your horn near blind pedestrians; it may startle or confuse them. Use horn only to avoid collisions.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you must:
options: a:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a cane or guide dog must be yielded to; stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: When visibility is very low due to fog, you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.
note: Use low beams and reduce speed in dense fog; if you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for conditions to improve.

question: When near a distracted driver, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:One to two seconds.,b:Two to three seconds.,c:Three to four seconds.,d:Less than one second.
note: Give distracted drivers extra space by maintaining a following distance of at least three to four seconds.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using siren and lights, what must you do?
options: a:Move to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stop immediately even if in an intersection.,c:Slow to the right lane and continue slowly.,d:Speed up and clear the way by passing.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by driving as far right as possible and stopping, avoiding stopping in intersections.

question: During rainy weather, when should you be most careful turning or stopping?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:During the first half hour of rain.,c:After it has been raining all day.,d:Only when puddles form.
note: The roadway is most slippery during the first 30 minutes of rain as oil and grime mix with water.

question: Yellow lines on the roadway separate:
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow centerlines mark two-way traffic; broken or solid patterns indicate where passing is permitted or prohibited.

question: When may you safely return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When the passed vehicle signals you to return.,d:After signaling for three seconds.
note: You should move back into your lane only after you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road, what is the right action?
options: a:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly.,b:Ease off the gas and stay off the brakes.,c:Shift into a lower gear immediately.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to correct it.
note: If you feel a loss of traction, ease off the accelerator and avoid braking or turning until traction returns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If facing a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, you should:
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: Do not enter an intersection you cannot clear; blocking intersections is illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Overtaking cars.,b:Oncoming cars.,c:No one.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles that are proceeding straight through the intersection.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do?
options: a:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,b:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection and then turn.,c:Turn without yielding to others.,d:Only yield to pedestrians.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: When being passed, maintain a steady speed and do not increase speed until the passing vehicle has safely re-entered your lane.

question: For how long do passenger restrictions apply to newly licensed drivers?
options: a:Three months.,b:Six months.,c:Twelve months.,d:Two months.
note: During the first six months, new drivers are limited to passengers who are driving instructors, parents/guardians, or licensed adults 20+ with certain restrictions.

question: If arrested for a first-time DUI and you refuse a breath test, your license will be suspended for at least:
options: a:14 days.,b:45 days.,c:21 days.
note: Refusing a chemical test results in an administrative suspension of at least 45 days and requirements for reinstatement.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered dangerous?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.,c:It draws the attention of other drivers.
note: Cell phone use while driving diverts the driver's eyes, hands, and attention, increasing crash risk.

question: When visibility is poor due to fog, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Turn your lights to their high beam setting.,c:Turn your lights to their low beam setting.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, snow or mist; high beams will reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Changing from one lane to another is best done:
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Change lanes gradually and deliberately after signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots; avoid frequent lane changes.

question: The conviction of a 16- or 17-year-old for violating the electronic device law may result in:
options: a:A $500 fine.,b:A 10-day suspension.,c:A 30-day suspension.
note: Drivers under 18 may face license suspension (at least 30 days) and retraining for violations of the electronic device restrictions.

question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: Reduce speed before entering curves and intersections; braking or sharp steering on slippery surfaces can cause a skid.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: Reduce your speed in wet, snowy, or icy conditions because tires have less traction on slippery surfaces.

question: At a railroad crossing you must do which of the following?
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings such as school buses and hazardous-materials trucks.,b:Watch for multiple trains.,c:Both of the above.
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution, watch for specialized vehicles that must stop, and be aware of the possibility of more than one train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:
options: a:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.,c:Both of the above.
note: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to traffic already circulating in the roundabout before entering.

question: How should you drive through a work zone?
options: a:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,c:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.
note: Slow down, obey posted speeds, watch for workers and changing conditions, and be ready to stop suddenly in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way road with a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line, what does this mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid one, traffic next to the dashed line may pass, but traffic next to the solid line may not.

question: When a school bus is stopped on the road ahead to load or unload children, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus cautiously.
note: Stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and extended stop arm until the red lights stop and the arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic before merging smoothly into the flow.

question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what is a safe assumption?
options: a:That the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,b:That the other driver will make room for you.,c:Do not assume other drivers will give you space to return to the lane.,d:That using your turn signal guarantees a safe pass.
note: Never assume other drivers will make space; check that you have room to pass and return safely.

question: On roadways, bicycles are legally considered:
options: a:Vehicles.,b:Hazards.,c:Dangerous.
note: Bicycles are vehicles and must follow the same traffic laws; drivers and bicyclists share the road.

question: After stopping for a train that has just passed, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,b:Look for a second train.,c:Both of the above.
note: Even after a train passes, watch for additional trains and wait until warning signals stop and gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: There is an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights and a siren. How should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and keep moving.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Pull over to the right and stop.
note: You must yield right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling as near to the right edge of the road as possible and stopping until they pass.

question: When taking any medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Consult your doctor about the effects before driving.,b:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,c:Have someone follow you home.
note: Ask your doctor or pharmacist how a prescription or over-the-counter drug may affect your driving, especially sedatives or tranquilizers.

question: What are 'No zones' around trucks?
options: a:Have sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,b:Disappear into blind spots or are so close that they restrict the truck driver's ability to stop and maneuver safely.,c:Have several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.
note: No zones are the large blind spots around trucks where smaller vehicles may disappear from the truck driver's view or be dangerously close.

question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio.,b:Constantly know what is happening around your vehicle.,c:Keep eyes fixed ahead only.,d:Drive with high beam headlights on.
note: Awareness of surroundings front, side, and rear helps you foresee hazards and avoid dangerous situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From where on a two-way street should you begin a left turn?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, begin from the lane closest to the centerline and turn into the first legal lane.

question: Before changing lanes you should check mirrors and:
options: a:Never look over your right shoulder.,b:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,c:Glance over your shoulder.
note: In addition to mirror checks, glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When the driver you passed signals you to return.,c:When you have signaled for three seconds.,d:When you are two car lengths ahead.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Always stop before entering.,b:Merge carefully into a safe gap in traffic.,c:Expect traffic to clear because you have the right-of-way.,d:Cross two lanes at once to reach the fast lane.
note: Identify a gap, adjust your speed to match traffic, signal, and merge carefully into that gap.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; large trucks have especially large blind spots that other drivers should avoid.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:An intersection,c:A bridge
note: Bridges and overpasses can freeze before the rest of the roadway and should be crossed with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red traffic light that displays a green arrow for your lane, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the light changes.,c:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: If you are in a lane controlled by a green arrow, you may make the movement indicated when the way is clear.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes.,b:Allowing your hands to let go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head against the head restraint.,d:Keeping a firm grip on the wheel.
note: If struck from behind, maintain a firm grip on the wheel and press your head into the head restraint; do not let go of the steering wheel.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: When available, wear both the lap and shoulder belts; using one part alone greatly reduces protection.

question: If you see a lane control sign showing an arrow with the word only below it, you should:
options: a:Travel in the direction of the arrow.,b:Always make a lane change.,c:Look for a destination sign to follow.
note: A lane control sign with an only arrow requires that traffic in that lane move in the direction indicated by the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the center of the road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line, and the broken line is next to your lane, what does that mean?
options: a:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,b:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.,c:You are in a passing zone and may pass on the left when no oncoming traffic is present.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to your lane, drivers in your lane may cross the centerline to pass when it is safe to do so; drivers next to the solid line may not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what actions should you take?
options: a:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:All of the above.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before any lane change or pass.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up to make the turn before it changes.,c:You do not need to signal to turn.,d:You have protected turning right.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the green-arrow protection is ending; yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

question: Roads are most slippery just after rain begins. In that situation you should:
options: a:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.,b:Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.,c:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.
note: After the first rain, reduce speed and avoid abrupt turns or stops because oil and residue make pavement especially slick.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe practice on the interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,b:Change lanes without signaling.,c:If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.
note: Always signal before changing lanes. If you miss an interstate exit, proceed to the next exit; do not back up or make U-turns.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving and is a leading factor in crashes.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,c:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must avoid striking pedestrians and must yield when necessary regardless of where or how the pedestrian is crossing.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is approaching while you are about to pass a pedestrian, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at the same speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.,d:Pass the pedestrian quickly between the oncoming vehicle and the pedestrian.
note: If an oncoming vehicle is approaching, deal with one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time and one is on your left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the vehicle to the right goes first. If the other car is to your left, you are to its right and have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive significantly slower than the flow of traffic, what may occur?
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving too slowly can obstruct normal traffic flow and may result in a citation if you impede other vehicles.

question: As daylight begins to fade, which lights should you use so others can see you?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Turn on your low beam headlights as daylight fades. Use high beams only in open areas where no other drivers are present.

question: When driving in fog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road safely and wait.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's bright headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Stop until the other driver passes.,c:Look below their headlights.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road and use the lane markings as a guide until the oncoming vehicle has passed.

question: Slowing down to look at collisions or other unusual events:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.
note: Avoid “rubbernecking.” Slowing to look at collisions often causes congestion and secondary crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,c:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

question: If you continually drive faster than surrounding vehicles and repeatedly pass on a two-lane road, what is most likely to happen?
options: a:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads increases your collision risk because each pass raises the chance of an accident.

question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, you should use:
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow to reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:So others can see your vehicle.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:To warn others of bad weather.,d:To increase interior visibility.
note: Use headlights in poor weather so other drivers can see your vehicle; if wipers are on, low beams must be used.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct approach to re-enter the roadway?
options: a:Turn immediately back onto the roadway sharply.,b:Wait until safe, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,c:Stop where you are and walk back onto the road.,d:Accelerate and jerk the wheel to return.
note: Reduce speed, check traffic, and when safe, gradually steer back onto the pavement to avoid losing control.

question: To check for vehicles in your blind spots you should look:
options: a:The inside rearview mirror.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:Over your shoulders.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors; look over your shoulders to check them before changing lanes.

question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill on a road without a curb, turn your wheels toward the side of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: When is it necessary to use your low-beam headlights?
options: a:When driving in fog.,b:When on a freeway.,c:When on a well-lit street.,d:When following another vehicle closely at any time.
note: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist because high beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: When driving through a construction zone you should:
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones often have changed lanes, workers, and equipment; drive cautiously and be prepared for unusual conditions.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, what is the safest action?
options: a:Slam on the brakes.,b:Not drive through the flooded area; turn around and find another route.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: Never drive through flooded roadways. Even shallow water can hide hazards or sweep a vehicle away; turn around and seek another route.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: Pentagonal school signs warn you that you are approaching a school zone or crossing; be alert and prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street only when traffic on that street flows left and no sign prohibits the turn.

question: If weather or light conditions require you to have lights on while driving, which lights should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your low beams.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain, fog, snow, or other reduced-visibility situations; high beams can reflect and reduce visibility.

question: You must show proof of insurance to a law enforcement officer when:
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry and present evidence of financial responsibility (insurance) whenever you drive and upon request after a stop or collision.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Never.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: Never go around or under a lowered railroad gate; wait until the gates are fully raised and it is safe to cross.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.,d:They have better visibility than cars.
note: Large trucks require much more distance to stop than passenger cars traveling at the same speed; a large truck can take nearly twice the stopping distance of a car at highway speeds.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction.,c:A construction zone is ahead.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and allows passing when the way is clear and safe.

question: Which of the following best defines a distraction while driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: A distraction is any activity or condition that diverts your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving and increases crash risk.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Stop, then enter when safe.,b:Yield to all traffic before crossing.,c:Slow down and proceed through carefully.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: How is alcohol classified in terms of its effect on the body?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.,d:A hallucinogen.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment, slows reflexes, and degrades driving ability.

question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, you must:
options: a:You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.,c:You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
note: Even on a green signal, yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, how should you enter the interstate?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and speed up to match the flow of traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.
note: Only accelerate into the interstate after you have identified a safe gap in traffic; do not use the shoulder to gain speed.

question: Reaction time is slower after which activity?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, impairs vision and judgment, and reduces driving ability.

question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a light.,c:When parked on a level roadway with no curb.,d:When stopped in traffic behind another car.
note: When parked on a slope, turn the wheels so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail; keep wheels straight when waiting to turn.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard continuous braking on ice or snow can lock wheels and cause loss of steering control; slow down and brake gently.

question: What must you do when you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway?
options: a:Change lanes immediately and keep speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment and slow down.,c:Stop in the travel lane to observe.,d:Speed up to pass the area quickly.
note: Slow down and be prepared for workers, slow equipment, or lane closures when entering a work zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting the freeway on a curved downhill ramp, you should:
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.,b:Wait until in the curve to begin braking.,c:Maintain freeway speed until the ramp levels out.,d:Accelerate slightly to maintain momentum.
note: Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve; braking within a curve can cause skidding.

question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. You should:
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.,c:Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; pedestrians may be crossing that you cannot see from your position.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do first?
options: a:Ease up on the gas pedal and steer in the direction of the skid.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Turn off the ignition immediately.,d:Shift into neutral and hold the wheel steady.
note: If you start to skid, release the accelerator or brake to help regain balance and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: What is the only reliable way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Take a cold shower.,c:Wait; allow time to pass.,d:Exercise vigorously.
note: Only time will remove alcohol from your system; food, coffee, showers, or exercise do not speed up alcohol elimination.

question: If a vehicle is following you too closely on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.
note: Slow down gradually or change lanes when safe; this encourages the tailgater to pass and reduces crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain speed and look both ways.,b:Slow, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,c:Stop only if other vehicles are nearby.,d:Proceed without stopping if you think it's clear.
note: If cross traffic is obscured, stop and inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing midblock instead of in a crosswalk, how should you respond?
options: a:Must stop for them.,b:Do not have to stop for them.,c:Should honk your horn at them.
note: You must yield to pedestrians and take all reasonable actions to avoid hitting them, even if they are not following traffic laws.

question: How would you describe backing up a vehicle?
options: a:Never dangerous.,b:Always dangerous.,c:Dangerous only for large vehicles.,d:Safe if you back up quickly.
note: Backing up is always hazardous because visibility is limited; use extra caution and helpers if available.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, you should:
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can entirely clear it; blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter highway traffic you should look for at least a:
options: a:A two-second gap.,b:A three-second gap.,c:A four-second gap.
note: You need a sufficiently large opening—about a four-second gap—to merge safely into traffic at highway speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:During rush hour traffic.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If you entered the intersection on the green light.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:Directly behind the body.,b:On the immediate left of the cab.,c:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on both sides and especially directly behind; if you cannot see the truck driver in the side mirror, the driver likely cannot see you.

question: When passing another vehicle on multi-lane roads, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead.,d:When the passed vehicle slows down.
note: Move back when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating sufficient space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, what is a recommended action?
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Check mirrors to be aware of traffic behind and around you before you apply the brakes for a smooth, safe stop.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large vehicles need greater stopping distance due to their mass; sudden stops in front of them increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with its red lights flashing must remain stopped until:
options: a:All students are off the bus.,b:The stop arm is retracted.,c:The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: Do not proceed until the school bus turns off its red lights, retracts the stop arm, and begins moving again.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are needed to affect your driving?
options: a:Three.,b:Two.,c:One.,d:None — only heavy drinking impairs you.
note: Even a single drink can impair driving ability; avoid driving after any alcohol consumption.

question: When backing out from an alley or driveway onto a sidewalk, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,c:Assume pedestrians will yield to vehicles.,d:Sound horn and proceed quickly.
note: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area when emerging from an alley, driveway, or parking lot to give pedestrians right-of-way.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, you should set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so a roll would move the vehicle away from traffic.

question: When is pavement most slippery during rain?
options: a:If it has been raining for one to two hours.,b:If it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining several hours.,d:After it stops raining.
note: Roads are especially slippery when rain first begins because oil and dirt mix with water to form a greasy film.

question: After you have held your license for six months, which passenger is NOT allowed in your vehicle?
options: a:Your 18-year-old friend.,b:Your parent(s).,c:Your younger brother.
note: Under Connecticut's graduated license restrictions, newly licensed drivers face passenger limits; non-family friends are restricted during early licensing periods.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Should drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,b:Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.
note: Wait for a sufficiently large gap so you can accelerate to the speed of traffic before merging safely into the lane.

question: What is the correct technique when backing up?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Press hard on the gas pedal to maneuver quickly.,c:Look through the rear window while backing slowly.,d:Close your eyes briefly to focus.
note: When backing, turn and look through the rear window and move slowly; do not depend solely on mirrors or speed.

question: To prevent becoming an aggressive driver you should:
options: a:Relax and concentrate on driving.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit.,c:Tailgate the driver in front of you.
note: Stay calm, focus on safe driving, allow extra travel time, and avoid reacting angrily to other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,b:Yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:Yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane means you may cross the centerline to pass when it is safe; a solid line next to you means you may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom do you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:On your left.,b:Who arrived before you.,c:Across from your vehicle.
note: Vehicles proceed in the order they arrived; yield to drivers who arrived before you at a stop-controlled intersection.

question: A pedestrian who started crossing after a 'Don't Walk' signal is in the intersection when your light turns green. What do you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.
note: You must yield to any pedestrian in the intersection; wait until they have cleared the roadway before going.

question: When a school bus is stopped on your side of the road with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights on your side of the road and remain stopped until the lights are off and the stop arm is retracted.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, what is required?
options: a:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Only proceed if you have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you should slow down, be alert for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

question: A school bus is stopped ahead of you in your lane with red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed when you think all of the children have exited the bus.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.
note: You must stop when a school bus on your side of the road has red flashing lights; remain stopped until the lights are turned off. On a divided highway, opposite-direction traffic may not have to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how do you know you have enough room to return to your lane?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,d:If you can no longer see the vehicle in your side mirror.
note: You may safely move back into the driving lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,b:Traffic control devices.,c:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas beside and just behind your vehicle that cannot be seen using mirrors; check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: In terms of its effect on the nervous system, alcohol is classified as which of the following?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a depressant; it slows nerve impulses and impairs concentration, coordination, and judgment.

question: What term refers to the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).,c:Implied consent (IC).,d:Alcohol impairment ratio (AIR).
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream; higher BAC means greater impairment.
